name: Battala woodcut
summary: A cheap woodcut sheet from the Battala bazaar quarter of Calcutta. Local craftsmen cut a bold black outline, often to copy a painted original, and printed it with type on thin country paper.

philosophy.core_thesis: A cheap wood block with a bold line can put a sacred or comic story in the hands of a bazaar crowd.
design_principles: Cut a strong, even outline in wood and keep the line 0.5–1.5 mm wide.
Fill large shapes with a flat colour, applied by hand or by a second block.
Show gods, village scenes and city satire, with the main figure at the centre.
Print the verse or the title in Bengali type on the same sheet.
Use thin country paper; do not hide its fibre.
Keep the hatch short and sparse, in the style of a European wood engraving that the cutter had seen.
Accept a thick line, a blot and a shift of 1–2 mm between the black and the colour.
anti_patterns: Smooth oil-like blend of the oleograph kind
Fine engraved line with deep shadows

process.matrix: A block of hard wood, cut along or across the grain.
process.press: A hand letterpress or a hand-rubbed print.
process.image_making: A Bengali craftsman cuts the block, often from a painted or a European original.
process.edition: Thousands of sheets from one block.

inks.strategy: One black ink for the outline; red and other colours are added by hand or by a second block.

screening.rule: Draw all form as an outline with sparse short hatch; make no tone with a screen.

registration.rule: The colour is often applied by hand, so it can sit 1–2 mm off the outline.

substrate.stock: A thin country paper, cream, with a coarse fibre.

surface.impression: A light bite on the soft paper, with the type pressed in a little.
surface.texture: Thick outline with a visible wood grain and thin, sparse hatch.

marks: type and picture on one sheet

evidence.title: Battala Jagannath
evidence.credit: Victoria and Albert Museum via Wikimedia Commons

emotion.target_response: Warm, plain humour and faith: the viewer sees a lively bazaar sheet.

use_cases: book and album covers with a Bengali theme
editorial images for South Asian history
avoid_when: The brief asks for a polished, glossy or photographic image.

modifiers.how: Replace the outline with a smooth painted blend in 6–10 colour stones and add a gloss varnish.
Replace the thick outline with fine parallel hatch and a tone built from line.
